vignette: Jude is a 20-year-old African American male who has recently returned from active duty in combat. Since his return, Jude has been struggling with symptoms that have significantly impacted his life as a doctor and his overall well-being. The traumatic event occurred during one of the quieter moments on patrol when an unexpected silence was broken by violent explosions. The sudden transition from tranquility to chaos left Jude breathless and disoriented. He has since found himself reacting sharply to these specific triggers—sudden silences, instances of violence, and episodes of breathlessness—which have become potent reminders of that traumatic day. Jude’s experience of the event is fragmented; he recalls disconnected pieces but cannot form a coherent narrative. There are significant gaps in his memory, moments where it feels as though critical parts of the experience have been erased entirely. Each time he tries to piece together what happened, memories push away before he can fully grasp them. This fragmentation has led Jude to question his own identity and trust in the world around him. He finds himself thinking, "I feel like I don't know myself anymore," as if the trauma has reshaped who he is fundamentally. The loss of a stable sense of self and shattered beliefs about how the world operates have made Jude hyper-vigilant. He feels the need to be constantly on guard, always anticipating danger. This hypervigilance amplifies his reactions to triggers; whenever he hears sudden silence or witnesses any form of violence, his breath catches in his throat, triggering a cascade of distressing memories and intense fear. His occupation as a doctor has become increasingly challenging due to these symptoms. In the hospital, moments of quiet can be particularly unsettling, causing Jude to feel an overwhelming sense of dread. He finds himself avoiding certain shifts or situations where silence might occur, leading to strained relationships with his colleagues and reduced job satisfaction. The fragmented nature of Jude’s memory and the gaps that he cannot fill have further contributed to his negative appraisals. The inability to reconstruct a clear narrative from the traumatic event has solidified his belief that the world is unpredictable and dangerous. Each time he pushes away memories before they can fully form, it reinforces his sense of identity loss and shattered beliefs. Jude’s struggle with these symptoms has become increasingly debilitating over time. The triggers exacerbate his negative appraisals, which in turn intensify his hypervigilance and disrupt his ability to recall the event coherently. This cycle has tightened around him, making it difficult for Jude to maintain a sense of normalcy or control. What finally brought Jude to seek help was a particularly harrowing experience at work where silence during an emergency led to a momentary lapse in focus. He realized then that his symptoms were not only affecting his personal life but also endangering the lives he had dedicated himself to save. Jude is most afraid of losing himself completely and becoming someone unrecognizable from who he used to be. At the same time, he hopes for a way to regain control over his memories and fears, to reclaim a sense of self that feels whole again. Through therapy, Jude aims to find a path toward healing and stability, hoping to rebuild his shattered beliefs and reconnect with a version of himself that has not been overtaken by trauma.
